analysis:
Both units are head-side text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md only (mode 100644, no rename). Excerpt 1 starts at line 389 and excerpt 2 at line 618. They contain documentation prose and no executable code, configuration, or security-control change, so I found no concrete security regression in them.

The entries describe behavior changes that touch the threat model. I could not check any of them because the implementing source is not in this batch:
- App Attest retry and recovery, MDM-optional serving, durable build qualification, and revocation fencing (TB-011, T-052..T-058, A-015..A-017). The text says retries never extend or grant authorization, and that serving stays disabled by default.
- Encrypted SSD prefix-cache defaults for Bonsai 2, Gemma QAT and GPT-OSS (T-041, SEC-035). The text keeps the global kill switch and the account-scoped salt.
- The 30-minute SSD cache TTL is in the canonical context, but the changelog still mentions a 100 GiB ceiling and 15-minute figures in older entries. Those older entries are historical.
- New payment and billing surface: Stripe Global Payouts, one-time model token grants, and sponsored-traffic settlement (TB-008, A-009, T-030). The changelog says these operations are atomic.
- Admin email login now JSON-encodes Privy OTP fields (TB-006).
- Prior-version fixes: SSE error completion, Responses media lowering, and negative max-token rejection.

The next pass should check the real code for these areas: coordinator/appattest/service, the registry authorization fence at final dispatch, the payouts and promotions ledger atomicity, and the SSD cache policy defaults. Do not treat the changelog claims as proof. The threat-model file may need updating for the new Global Payouts route and the model token grant ledger, but that cannot be confirmed from a changelog alone.
